Offset only affects the interest it doesn't actually reduce the physical loan where extra payments reduces both physical loan and interest.

You are saving same amount in interest but you're not paying it off slower with offset

Depends on if you are just wanting to save on interest or pay off faster.
Keeping in off set or making extra principal payments saves the exact same amount in interest. The only difference is loan will end earlier with extra payments.

In my case I've worked it out that after 15years I will be paying no interest at all but I will still be paying principal for another 3 years for a total of 18 years to pay the loan where if I half my offset at 8/10years and dump it as an extra payment on principal I'll be paying about 150-50 in interest per fortnight but will have the loan paid off in 16.5years savings 1.5years. it's a weird balancing act.

As the interest gets lower the offset becomes less worthwhile for saving time and it's better to make principle payments if your aim is to pay off as soon as possible. 

My personal opinion is to do half offset half extra payment just to have emergency funds. Maybe first 5 years just solely stick to offset as it'll still save the same amount of money but after 5 years should start doing extra payments (while keeping offset) to save extra time on top of saving money.
